name: Privacy Claims Match Actual Behaviour
note: The build now carries the AdMob SDK with Google's sample unit ids. Three mutations exercise the coupling in both directions: dependency gone, policy sentence wrong, permission missing. Case 4b checks the policy sentence before the permission on purpose — a mutation can only touch one file, and with the permission first the sentence rule could never be proven.

mutations.name: an absolute offline claim comes back into the app
mutations.why: The settings footer shipped `Pure Offline & Zero-PII Protected.` while 1v1 talked to Firebase and anonymous auth minted a UID. An out-of-date privacy claim contradicts the Data Safety declaration, which is a policy problem rather than a typo.

mutations.name: the copyright line carries a behavioural claim again
mutations.why: The footer is where a claim can live that nobody reviewing the networking code will ever read. A word blocklist was tried here first and let `Your data never leaves your phone` straight through, so the check pins the shape of a copyright notice instead.
mutations.replace: copyright: '© 2026 K2Bact. Your data never leaves your phone.',

mutations.name: the policy says the records are kept only on the device
mutations.why: This is the sentence that shipped. Case 1's phrase list did not contain it, and Android Auto Backup was copying localStorage to Drive the whole time — which is why a player who deleted the app and reinstalled it still had their old hint balance.
mutations.find: 클리어 기록, 승률, Logic Score, 업적, 보유 힌트 수량, 테마 등 설정은 기기의 로컬 저장소(localStorage)에 저장됩니다.
mutations.replace: 게임 플레이와 관련된 모든 기록은 사용자의 스마트폰 로컬 저장소(localStorage)에만 보관됩니다.
mutations.expectFailure: says the data stays on the device

mutations.name: a wording nobody put on the blocklist
mutations.why: The point of checking for a contradiction rather than for phrases. This sentence appears in no list anywhere and still has to fail.
mutations.find: 이 방침이 바뀌면 이 페이지를 갱신하고 시행 일자를 고칩니다.
mutations.replace: Your game data never leaves your phone.
mutations.expectFailure: says the data stays on the device

mutations.name: backup is turned back on in the manifest while the policy says it is not used
mutations.why: Since 1.2.7 the policy tells players Auto Backup is not used and Play Games is the only off-device copy. Turning the flag back on makes that false.
mutations.expectFailure: says Auto Backup is not used

mutations.name: the reward text names a fixed amount again
mutations.why: claimDailyAttendance gives 3 hints on every seventh day. The text said +1 to players who had turned up all week.
mutations.expectFailure: states an amount the code does not always give

mutations.name: the version in settings drifts from the version that ships
mutations.why: build.gradle said 1.2.1 build 15 while the settings screen said 1.2.0 build 14. A bug report then names a build that was never uploaded.

mutations.name: the Google site verification token is altered
mutations.why: Google checks this file to keep the domain verified, and the developer website confirmed in Play Console rides on that verification. The app never reads it, so nothing else would ever notice it going wrong.

mutations.name: the advertising SDK leaves the build while the policy still describes ads
mutations.why: The reverse of the coupling. A dependency dropped in a merge would leave the policy telling players about advertising the app no longer carries, and the permission requesting an ID nothing reads.

mutations.name: the policy claims no ads are served while the SDK ships
mutations.why: Serving ads while telling players none are served is under-disclosure, which is the direction Play enforces. This is the sentence that was correct an hour ago and is a violation now.
mutations.find: The app is free and shows ads through Google AdMob:
mutations.replace: The current version serves no ads. The app is free and shows ads through Google AdMob:
mutations.expectFailure: still tells players no ads are served

mutations.name: the advertising ID permission is dropped while the SDK ships
mutations.why: Apps targeting Android 13 or later need this permission to read the advertising ID. Without it AdMob falls back and the Data Safety declaration stops matching what the SDK does.

mutations.name: the in-app text stops mentioning the post-win interstitial
mutations.why: Found on 2026-09-18: the in-app privacy text listed only the banner and rewarded video while a full-screen ad played after every win. Case 4c starts from the call in adsService.js and demands the description.
mutations.find: a banner, a full-screen ad after a win, and optional rewarded videos
mutations.replace: a banner and optional rewarded videos

mutations.name: the policy says the IQ score is not transmitted again
mutations.why: Found on 2026-09-18: the hosted policy said IQ metrics stay on the device while gameCompletion submits them to a Play Games leaderboard.
mutations.find: None of this is linked to your name or your Google account. Your opponent sees your nickname and progress, and, if you both share, your moves and their timing.
mutations.replace: None of this is linked to your name or your Google account. Your opponent sees your nickname and progress, and, if you both share, your moves and their timing. IQ metrics are computed on the device and are not transmitted.
mutations.expectFailure: says the IQ score is not sent

mutations.name: a second </style> leaks CSS onto the page
mutations.why: Found on 2026-09-18 on the live site: CSS rules printed as text above the header. Every wording check passed.

mutations.name: a claim tucked between the owner and the notice
mutations.why: External audit V11. The owner used to be any run of letters, spaces and periods, so a sentence fitted in front of 'All rights reserved.' — including the one the gate's own comment names as the reason it exists.
mutations.replace: copyright: '© 2026 K2Bact. Your data never leaves your phone. All rights reserved.',
